svg.title: Inside one decoder block: the residual stream runs left to right as a horizontal line, with RMSNorm, the Q/K/V projection, RoPE, attention with the causal mask and softmax, and the output projection hanging off it, then a second RMSNorm and the SwiGLU MLP, each sublayer adding its result back into the stream
svg.desc: One decoder block, drawn as a residual stream. A horizontal line runs left to right: x, one HiddenSize-wide row per position, the block's only long-lived state. The block body is composeSeqBlock (internal/model/forward.go:826); the per-sublayer wiring is composeSeqSublayer (forward.go:847), which for the default PreNorm topology computes x += body(norm(x)). The first sublayer hangs off the stream: normSeq (forward.go:810) applies RMSNorm, SerialRMSNorm (internal/model/norm/scalar.go:23), then attnSeq (forward.go:621) does the Q/K/V projection as three matrix multiplies, newRopeForLayer (forward.go:442) and rope.apply (forward.go:452) rotate Q and K by position, the score is dot(q,k) times attnScale, the causal mask is a loop bound so position t never scores past t, softmaxInPlace (forward.go:924) normalizes the scores, the values are weighted and summed, and the output projection o_proj mixes the heads back down to HiddenSize. That delta is added back into the stream at a residual add. The second sublayer hangs off the updated stream: a second normSeq, then mlpSeq (forward.go:793), which calls denseSwiGLU (internal/model/moe.go:140) — gate_proj, up_proj, silu, elementwise multiply, down_proj — and its delta is added back at a second residual add. The two residual adds are what make the block a stream: each sublayer computes a change to add, never a replacement, so the shape never changes. The decode twin of this block is blockStep (internal/model/kv.go:917), the same wiring over one position.
svg.text: Inside one decoder block — the residual stream
Two sublayers hang off one horizontal line. Each computes a delta and adds it back; nothing overwrites the stream. That is what makes it a stream.
one HiddenSize-wide row per position · mutated in place · shape never changes
block body: composeSeqBlock (forward.go:826) · wiring: composeSeqSublayer (forward.go:847) · default PreNorm: x += body(norm(x))
score = dot(q,k) × attnScale → causal mask (loop bound: t never scores past t) → softmax
→ weights → Σ wᵢ·Vᵢ → o_proj (concat heads, back to HiddenSize)
GQA: GroupSize = NumHeads / NumKVHeads queries share one KV head (config.go:1692)
g = gate_proj(xn) → silu(g) · u = up_proj(xn) · activated = silu(g) * u
Each sublayer computes a change and adds it back — x += body(norm(x)).
Nothing overwrites the stream, so the shape never changes and the
information accumulates. The two (+) circles are the residual adds.
· ParallelResidual (GPT-NeoX), where both sublayers read the original
stream and both deltas land in one add. Chosen by BlockTopology (arch.go:691).
The same block exists twice: composeSeqBlock (forward.go:826) for whole-sequence prefill, and blockStep (kv.go:917) for one-token decode. The wiring is
shared; only the data shape differs. The two must compute the same function — the RMSNorm arithmetic, the RoPE rotation, the GQA sharing, the softmax,
the residual adds, and the SwiGLU — or a token generated during decode would not match the same token scored during prefill. The f32 path is pinned
bit-exact against the prefill path, and the decode path's RoPE funnels through ropeRowQK (kv.go:1070) so a convention change lands in one place.
Attention mixes across positions; the MLP transforms within a position; the residual stream carries everything forward. Every modern decoder is a stack of this block.
